Stein Leonid - master of attack.pdf

Stein–Korchnoi (USSR International Grandmaster)
Zonal, Moscow 1964
Sicilian Defence
1 P–K4 P–QB4 2 N–KB3 P–Q3 3 P–Q4 PxP 4 NxP N–KB3 5 N–QB3
P–QR3 6 B–K2 P–K3 7 0–0 B–K2 8 P–B4 Q–B2 9 Q–K1 0–0
10 Q–N3 Q–N3 (Korchnoi has often shown his readiness to submit to an
attack in return for slight material gain. Even in this ultimately disastrous
case it is not clear that his decision was incorrect.) 11 B–K3 QxP 12 B–B2
Q–N5 13 P–K5 PxP 14 PxP N–K1 15 B–Q3 Q–R4 16 N–K4 (Stein’s
pieces converge menacingly against Black’s King.) 16 ... N–Q2 17 N–KB3
P–KN3 18 B–Q4 N–N2 19 N–B6+ BxN 20 PxB N–R4 21 Q–R4 Q–Q1
22 QR–K1 N/2xP 23 N–N5 (Threatening 24 RxN NxR 25 BxN Q-N3+ 26
K-R1 P–KR4 27 QxP! PxQ 28 B–R7 mate. “With Steinitzian skill
Korchnoi returns both his extra pawns to demonstrate that his position is
still tenable,”—Cozens.) 23...P-K4! 24 BxKP P-R3 BxN PxN 26 QxP
NxB 27 RxN Q–Q5+ 28 K-R1 Q–KN5 29 Q–R6 B–B4 30 P–KR3
Q–Q5? (The Great Defender goes astray. Correct was 30 ... Q–N5! gaining
an important tempo.) 31 RxB!! PxR 32 R–K3 Q–N2 33 Q–R4 Q–R8+
34 K-R2 KR-K1 (Staving off immediate calamity, but for the next
twelve moves until the end of the game Korchnoi is only permitted to
move his King.) 35 R–N3+ K–B1 36 Q–R6+ K–K2 37 R–K3+ K–Q2 38
BxP+ K–B2 39 Q–B4+ K–B3 40 Q–B4+ K–Q3 41 Q–N4+ K–Q4 42
R–Q3+ K–K4 43 Q–Q6+

43...KxB 44 R–B3+ K–N4 45 Q–B4+ K–R4 46 P–N4+ K–N3 47 QxP+
and Black resigned.
